Lessons.Title: Fractions on Number Lines
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 First Edition IM Grade4 Unit2 Lesson5 — Fractions on Number Lines. Original teacher Preparation, Lesson and student task PDF four pages inspected, including original diagrams on PDF pages2–3. Correct lesson goal and introduction preserved.
Warm-up Number Talk (10 min) mental products2×12=24,4×12=48,8×12=96,16×12=192. Describe a doubling strategy.

Activity1 All Lined Up (20 min) source page2: original four equal-length number lines label far-right endpoint2/2,4/4,8/8,12/12. All equal1 and center points represent1/2,2/4,4/8,6/12. Source page3 set a quarter1/4=2/8=3/12=25/100, set b fifth1/5=2/10=20/100, set c two-thirds2/3=4/6=8/12. Count equal subdivisions and label SAME point. Teacher reviews diagrams and partner explanation, including why not to assume a first tick is1/10 without checking partitions.

Activity2 How Far to Run (15 min), original story: Han suggests3/4 mile; Kiran9/12 mile is equal because3/4=9/12. Tyler suggests7/8 mile, a DIFFERENT and longer run:3/4=6/8<7/8. Locate both on appropriately partitioned original number line. Teacher reviews correct drawing and justification.

Lesson synthesis (10 min): Equivalent fractions indicate equal distance from0 on identically scaled number lines;1/5 and10/50 are equivalent. Clarify number-line scale, unit length and partitions before giving fraction label.

First-party Edulytics Cool-down (5 min) in place of inaccessible educator-gated publisher original: demonstrate2/3=4/6 on two aligned lines and explain why7/8 is NOT3/4. Teacher evaluates full mathematical argument. Existing exact equivalence Practice tests supplementary numeric decisions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent line points
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fraction names may differ while indicating the SAME number-line location.
KeyConcepts.Rule: a/b=c/d when a×d=b×c, with positive denominators and matching unit wholes.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal scale
KeyConcepts.Definition: Each number line labels equally spaced parts of one same-sized whole.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Match distance from0, not just endpoint denominator labels.

KeyConcepts.Title: Different running distance
KeyConcepts.Definition: Not all fractions whose numerators/denominators look related are equivalent.
KeyConcepts.Example: Tyler runs 1/8 mile farther than Han/Kiran.

WorkedExamples.Title: One quarter across four number lines
WorkedExamples.Question: Give four names for the same quarter point.
WorkedExamples.Method: Partition matching unit wholes into4,8,12,100 parts.

WorkedExamples.Title: Run after school
WorkedExamples.Question: Do Han3/4 and Kiran9/12 propose the same run? And Tyler7/8?
Steps: 7/8>6/8, so Tyler proposes a longer distance.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Han and Kiran same; Tyler different.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independently authored Grade 4 lesson reasoning
WorkedExamples.Question: Which labels coincide with the 3/4 mark on a 0-to-1 number line: 6/8 or 7/8?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact relationship and representation requested by this lesson.
Steps: Double numerator and denominator of 3/4 to obtain 6/8.
WorkedExamples.Check: First-party mathematically checked model. Original publisher activity and student drawings require independent teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using endpoint10/10 to label any first visible marked point1/10.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The actual line interval divisions determine point value.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Count EQUAL tick intervals from0 to1 and point position.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming9/12 differs from3/4 because the digits are different.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Numerator and denominator are both multiplied by3.

SummaryPoints: Original Number Talk times12 and four right endpoint/halfpoint lines.
Source page3 fraction equivalence groups1/4,1/5,2/3 plus shared endpoints.
Han3/4=Kiran9/12, while Tyler7/8 differs and is longer.
Teacher manually evaluates source geometry of number lines, explanations and run-distance discussion.
